title: Bound fixed caller queries and two-ADD HOST repairs
body:
## Results

Follow-up to #7098, with three independently runnable replay suites.

- The pinned #7000 central interval needs four rank-one QUERYs per branch when the boundary operator is fixed. The whole-caller lower bound under the inherited two-shear native factorization is three per branch. Even granting one deletion per branch for pricing, the #7004 complex moment is approximately −462.571 at κ = .005. The unchanged #7001 BIT moment is approximately −444.063.
- The pinned #6824 normalized word admits no specified same-port HOST repair through up to two added coframed ADDs across its 104 ports. This covers the existing chronology.
- The normalized #7002 projector schedule reduces 181 idle jobs to 75 per port, versus 76 in #7098. Its F+H1 raw complex moment is still approximately −814.904 at .005. The physical packed IDLE, precision, BIT and outer obligations remain.

No new κ claim. The README identifies where changing the native macro or entrance would escape these bounds.

## Reproduction

`python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/fixed-caller-query-and-host-limits`

The replay uses exact source pins and checks the fixed-interval sign ranks, retained-factorization bound, transport screen, projector schedule and rational tariffs, and the fixed-chronology HOST census. The normalized #6824 word is a generated input whose endpoint and inventory are checked during replay.
